subject: A question about the result of ProcD.lm

messages.author: 0115fa6682bc8072
messages.subject: A question about the result of ProcD.lm
parts:
Dear all,

I tried to repeat the example given in the A Practical Companion to Geometric Morphometrics for Biologists in order to practice using Procrustes ANOVA to test differences between the group means. The example I did was the use of the "apes" data in the "shapes" package. The code is from Chapter 8 statistics

data("apes")
#There is something wrong with specimen #60 so we'll leave it out
apes.dat <- apes$x[,,-60]
apes.proc <- gpagen(apes.dat)
apes.shape <- apes.proc$coords
apes.species <- as.factor(c(rep("gor",59),rep("chimp",53),rep("orang",54)))  #59 gorilla, 53 chimpanzees, 54 orangutans
anova.apes <- procD.lm(apes.shape~apes.species, iter = 999)
anova.apes

The result is an ANOVA table: 
                        Df        SS          MS             Rsq          F             Z             Pr(>F)   
apes.species   2       0.47304    0.23652     0.46273    70.193    8.4029     0.001 **
Residuals        163   0.54924    0.00337     0.53727                        
Total                165   1.02228                                        
---
Signif. codes:  0 ‘***’ 0.001 ‘**’ 0.01 ‘*’ 0.05 ‘.’ 0.1 ‘ ’ 1

I thought that the p-value should be relatively constant regardless of the number of permutations. However, when I changed the permutation number from 999 to 9999, only the p-value decreases by 10 folds as 0.0001 while the mean square and F value remains constant. Is it because the F test statistic is too large relative to the random sampling F values?

Thank you very much for looking at my question!

Best regards,
Charles Zhang

messages.author: aab55242ff4da6c6
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] A question about the result of ProcD.lm
parts:
Charles,

1/1000 = 0.001
1/10000 = 0.0001

P.values are estimates of the true probability of a type I error (finding the observed result in a distribution of all possible random results), which if estimated by a resampling procedure, is constrained by the number of permutations.  It will be rather constant, given a sufficient number of permutations, if the observed result is not extreme (at the tail of the distribution).  For example, a P-value of 0.35 should scale to approximately 0.350, 0.3500, etc.  In your case, 0.001 means none of the 999 random permutations exceeded the observed case; 0.0001 means none of the 9999 random permutations exceeded the observed case.

Mike
